newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover down in week to April 25.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover down in week to April 25.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) reported on Tuesday a 27.73 percent decline in its turnover during the week ending April 25, with bourse activity dominated by commercial paper ahead of Orthodox Easter weekend.
Total turnover fell to 34.324 million dinars ($6.06 million) from 47.495 million a week ago. The number of transactions rose to 251 from 230.
Traders said market participants remained on the sidelines ahead of the long Easter weekend and the upcoming May 1st Labour day two-day holiday.
"It was mainly companies who borrowed heavily ahead of holidays to raise funds either to pay out salaries or to clear previous liabilities. Otherwise, it was a dull week," a trader told Reuters.
For the week ending April 25 the BSE reported the following details:
* Commercial paper traded 242 times for a total of 33.369 million dinars.
* Treasury bills accounted for 8 transactions worth 0.517 million dinars.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged between an annual 331 and 520 percent, while maturity stood between seven and 30 days.
* The central bank continued to sell part of its bond portfolio on the secondary market. It sold 0.438 million dinars worth of bonds issued by the Serbian Commodity Reserve Agency.
* There was no trade in the central bank short-term bonds.
* Over-the-counter trade in commercial paper and treasury bills rose to 26.478 million dinars from 24.673 million a week ago.
* OTC trade in giro money, with banks trading their surplus liquidity, surged to 22.8 million dinars from 15.1 million a week ago.
